To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the β-decay properties of the neutron-rich Tl isotopes and Bi isotopes beyond the N = 126 shell closure have been measured for the first time, and that the half-lives are systematically underestimated by theoretical models.

We have measured for the first time the beta decay half-lifes of 219Bi and 211, 212, 213Tl isotopes, which are important for astrophysical r-process calculations, by means of an innovative experimental technique, developed for experiments in a high-background condition.
we measured the half-lives of neutron-rich Tl isotopes for the first time, and that the measured values are significantly larger than the ones predicted by theoretical models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and decay of neutron-rich nuclei far from stability.
the study of neutron-rich isotopes around the Pb region.
the investigation of the structure and decay properties of nuclei close to the doubly magic nucleus lead, in the region of the so-called r-process path.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the r-process calculations underestimate the half-lives of nuclei around N=126.
the half-lives of neutron-rich Bi and Tl isotopes are not yet fully understood.
there are significant deviations between the experimental and theoretical results, which are not yet understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the β-decay rates of nuclei in the region of the r-process are not yet well understood.
the experimental half-lives are systematically longer than the theoretical predictions.
the experimental results are in contradiction with theoretical predictions for the r-process, which are not able to reproduce the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the β-decay rates are enhanced by about a factor of 2 in the vicinity of 126 neutron number, which is not reproduced by the models.
the half-lives of neutron-rich Bi and Tl isotopes are significantly shorter than predicted by the state-of-the-art theoretical models.
a systematic investigation of β-decay rates of neutron-rich nuclei around lead is needed in order to provide reliable input for the r-process calculations.
